subject: ophthalmology
title: Diseases of the eyelids

steps.tx: **Blepharitis** inflames lid margins in anterior (staphylococcal ulcerative with collarettes and madarosis, or seborrhoeic squamous with greasy scales) and posterior (meibomian gland dysfunction with capped orifices and frothy tears) patterns. Chronicity breeds styes, chalazia, marginal keratitis and dry eye. Management is lid hygiene first (warm compresses melting meibum, scrubs, massage), short topical antibiotics for infective flares, and systemic doxycycline or azithromycin for posterior disease with rosacea. Demodex mites (cylindrical dandruff at lash bases) need tea tree based lid care.
steps.say: Crusty lashes need heat and scrubs before antibiotics. Frothy tears and capped oil glands mean posterior disease.

steps.tx: Gland lumps separate by pain and wall: **hordeolum externum (stye)** is an acute painful staphylococcal abscess of lash follicle or Zeiss gland pointing at the margin, while **hordeolum internum** strikes meibomian glands pointing inward; both get heat and usually drain spontaneously, with incision only for pointing persistence. **Chalazion** is a chronic painless sterile lipogranuloma of blocked meibomian gland (firm tarsal nodule, conjunctival granuloma inside), treated conservatively, then steroid injection or incision and curettage through conjunctiva. Recurrent or atypical chalazion in older adults needs histology to exclude sebaceous carcinoma masquerade.
steps.say: Painful margin lump is stye; painless tarsal lump is chalazion. Recurrent chalazion in elderly earns a biopsy.

steps.tx: Lid malpositions threaten cornea by exposure or lash trauma: **entropion** turns the margin inward (involutional from horizontal laxity and retractor disinsertion, cicatricial from trachoma or burns, spastic after surgery, congenital), while **ectropion** everts it (involutional medial ectropion with punctal eversion and watering, paralytic from facial palsy, cicatricial). Trichiasis (misdirected lashes) and distichiasis (extra posterior row) abrade cornea causing ulcers; epilation is stopgap, with electrolysis, cryotherapy or lid surgery definitive. Facial palsy lagoons the eye, needing taping, lubricants and often gold weight or tarsorrhaphy.
steps.say: Lashes touching cornea ulcerate it. Palsy that cannot close the eye needs taping and weights, not waiting.

steps.tx: **Ptosis** droops the upper lid (margin reflex distance under 2 mm): aponeurotic (involutional, high crease, levator function preserved), myogenic (levator weakness), neurogenic (third nerve with down and out eye, Horner with miosis and anhidrosis), mechanical (mass or oedema) and pseudoptosis (phthisis, contralateral retraction). Levator resection suits fair function; frontalis sling bypasses poor function (congenital, Marcus Gunn jaw winking). Commonest lid malignancy is **basal cell carcinoma** (lower lid, pearly rolled edge with telangiectasia), excised with margin control; sebaceous carcinoma mimics recurrent chalazion and demands map biopsies.
steps.say: Droop with small pupil and no sweat is Horner. Pearly lower lid ulcer with vessels is basal cell.
